meta_title: NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Inverse Trig Q9 Solution
meta_desc: NCERT Exemplar Class 12 inverse trig Q9: prove 2 tan-1(cos θ) = tan-1(2 cosec θ) gives θ = π/4. Full steps plus a free 8-question quiz to practise.

quiz.title: Inverse Trig Equations Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the double-angle identity for tan inverse and on solving inverse-trig equations like this NCERT Exemplar problem. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: For |x| < 1, 2 tan⁻¹ x equals which of the following?
questions.explanation: The double-angle identity is 2 tan⁻¹ x = tan⁻¹(2x/(1 − x²)) for |x| < 1. It comes from tan(2A) = 2 tan A/(1 − tan² A) with A = tan⁻¹ x.

questions.q: Applying that identity to 2 tan⁻¹(cos θ) gives tan⁻¹ of what expression?
questions.explanation: Put x = cos θ: 2x/(1 − x²) = 2 cos θ/(1 − cos² θ) = 2 cos θ/sin² θ, since 1 − cos² θ = sin² θ.

questions.q: The right-hand side term 2 cosec θ can be rewritten as:
Equating the two arguments, 2 cos θ/sin² θ = 2/sin θ simplifies to:
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by sin² θ and divide by 2: cos θ/sin² θ = 1/sin θ gives cos θ = sin θ.

questions.q: From cos θ = sin θ, the value of tan θ is:
questions.explanation: Dividing cos θ = sin θ by cos θ gives 1 = tan θ, so tan θ = 1.

questions.q: The value of θ in the interval (0, π/2) with tan θ = 1 is:
The identity 2 tan⁻¹ x = tan⁻¹(2x/(1 − x²)) holds without adjustment when:
questions.explanation: The plain identity is valid only for −1 < x < 1. Outside that range you must add or subtract π to keep the principal value correct.

questions.q: The general solution of tan θ = 1, with n any integer, is:
questions.explanation: tan has period π, so tan θ = 1 = tan(π/4) gives θ = nπ + π/4 for any integer n.

faq.q: Which identity is the key to this NCERT Exemplar problem?
faq.a: The double-angle result 2 tan⁻¹ x = tan⁻¹(2x/(1 − x²)), valid for |x| < 1. Setting x = cos θ turns the left side into a single tan inverse you can match against the right side.

faq.q: Why does 1 − cos² θ become sin² θ in the working?
faq.a: It uses the Pythagorean identity sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, which rearranges to 1 − cos² θ = sin² θ. That step collapses the denominator neatly to sin² θ.

faq.q: How does the equation reduce to tan θ = 1?
faq.a: After equating arguments you reach cos θ/sin² θ = 1/sin θ. Cancelling one sin θ gives cos θ = sin θ, and dividing by cos θ gives tan θ = 1.

faq.q: Is θ = π/4 the only answer, or are there more?
faq.a: π/4 is the principal solution in (0, π/2). Because tan repeats every π, the full set is θ = nπ + π/4 for any integer n, which is why the question mentions n.
